# Build — from an issue to a PR standing at the gate

**Nature: Transmuter** for machinery, **Conjurer** for canon/governance, **Enhancer** for product
code; the mode is named at § 3, and said aloud when it switches mid-run.

> **Give me an issue; I give you back a PR that is `CON-32`-Ready at its human gate — or a G5 stop
> saying exactly why it could not get there.**

**Everything after the first PR appears is [`sharingan`](../sharingan/SKILL.md)'s engine** —
readiness, unblocking channels, reviewer rounds and the escalation ladder, inherited, never restated;
sharingan wins on PR mechanics, this skill on what precedes a PR. **Hatsu has no CI plane to route a
released issue to** ([`docs/WORKFLOW.md`](../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § *Building an issue with no CI
plane*): Kurapika builds it himself in the mode § 3 confirms, stopping at **G5** where a local session
structurally cannot, never pretending a wake occurred.

**The phases this composite calls skip their own `## 0.`**
([`docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md`](../../../docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md) § 4); the plugin root is
[PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Authority every phase shares*.

## 1. Invocation

```
/build <product|repo_code>#<issue_number>
nen parse build --grammar "<code>#<n>" --line "<the raw invocation>"
nen repo resolve <CODE> --repo <the target repo's own checkout>
```

Case-insensitive; **a code is resolved, never guessed**. A missing argument or configuration item is
asked for and set up inline (`missing-argument`, `missing-configuration`;
[`WORKFLOW.md`](../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § 4 *Ask, set up, continue*): `nen parse` exit `2` or an
unresolved code is the trigger, the registered codes the options, an absent entry set up in
`nen/repos.json`. **If `#<N>` is a PR, hand straight to
[`sharingan`](../sharingan/SKILL.md) and say so** — § 2's `chain-position` **is** the issue-vs-PR
check: its (and `nen issue terminus`'s) exit `1` `{ issue, refused: true, reason }` is **the signal,
not a failure**. **Say the run started**: it holds a bounded `CON-25` delegation (§ 5), and an
unannounced delegation is one nobody can end.

**A target with no delivery-stage taxonomy** is [`docs/WORKFLOW.md`](../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md)
§ *A target repository with no delivery-stage taxonomy*: **never manufacture a `--chain-labels` map, never apply a nonexistent stage label**, and
that path creates **no G1 or label authority**.

## 2. Read the issue before touching it — where is it on the chain?

```bash
nen issue chain-position --target <owner/name> --issue <N> --repo <the target checkout> \
  --chain-labels "idea=<label>,researched=<label>,approved-team=<label>,approved-direct=<label>,\
building=<label>,in-review=<label>,epic=<label>"
```

`--chain-labels` is **caller data** — the target's own label names per role, from its
`nen/labels.json`, never guessed. **Map `building`, `in-review`, `idea` and `epic`**, the four that
decide whether an unmatched issue is really `routable`; the rest return under `unmappedRoles`,
blocking nothing, so **omit a role the repository lacks**, never a placeholder. An unknown role name
is exit `2`, **never guessed past**.

| `chain-position` reports | First move |
|---|---|
| `closed` | **The run ends**, naming what closed it and which PR delivered it |
| `building` | Released, open PR or not (`in-review` folds in) → § 4 |
| `idea` | Wake **Gon** to decompose it into an epic; his grammar unratified, he hands it back |
| `epic-awaiting-approval` | **Stop at G1** (row `mode-label`): the mode label is the maintainer's (`CON-4`) |
| `epic-approved` | Children advance wave by wave — § 4 |
| `routable` | Confirm the mode (§ 3), release it (§ 4), then build it |
| `undecidable` | **Never guess**: ask for the missing role's label, re-run — a role the repository lacks is omitted, never invented |

`epic-approved` folds both mode labels into one state — read which off the issue's labels;
`researched` is an **input role name**, never an output state.

## 3. The mode is confirmed before anything is released

The issue's `bankai:agent/*` scope label chooses Kurapika's **mode**, not a CI agent.

| Label present | Mode |
|---|---|
| `bankai:agent/naruto` — a constitution/governance (`CON-{n}`) change | **Conjurer** |
| `bankai:agent/yamamoto` — a handbook / Stack Matrix / schema / agent-def change | **Conjurer** |
| `bankai:agent/kisuke` — machinery only, sanctioned by an existing rule | **Transmuter** |
| several, spanning lanes | a `CON-36` chore on an `integration/<chore>` branch where it needs more than one PR — say so in the ask; the delivery PR is then `integration/<chore> → main` |

**With none, propose one and ask** — a wrong mode makes a plausible, wrongly shaped PR: a
**`DECIDE`** per [`jutaisho`](../jutaisho/SKILL.md) § 4, row `mode-unknown`, once per run. **A G1
stop is never a mode question**: for an unapproved epic the ask is the mode *label* (integration-branch
team delivery or direct-to-main), and **only the maintainer applies it** (`CON-4`).

## 4. Driving the whole chain, and releasing into it

An epic is followed all the way down.

1. **Gon decomposes** the idea into an epic with sequenced children (§ 2), watched in session.
2. **G1 is the maintainer's**: stop (`nen stop --gate G1 …`), brief the epic, ask for the mode label;
   nothing below happens until it exists.
3. **Waves advance — always this run's job**; Hatsu has no epic-coordinator workflow.
4. **Release** the issue into `building` — the G1-M go-signal (`CON-25`).
5. **Kurapika builds it himself, in this session, in the confirmed mode.**
6. **Each child's PR is driven** by [`sharingan`](../sharingan/SKILL.md)'s engine to `CON-32`
   readiness — `nen pr ready`'s verdict, never eyeballed.

**Step 4's label command, its `CON-25` carve-out and `CON-9`'s one stage label are
[`docs/WORKFLOW.md`](../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § *Releasing an issue into `building`***; every
application is logged: object, label, time.

**Steps 3, 5 and 6's machinery — waves, the terminus PR, the `--local-cap 2` slots, the `nen shu`
sequence and its G5 — is that document's § *Building an issue with no CI plane***.

## 5. Authority — what this run may and may not do

`CON-25`'s fourth carve-out: a human-invoked skill run holds the delegation its purpose requires,
**logged, run-scoped, and those label classes only**.

| | |
|---|---|
| **May release** | the `building` stage label on the named issue and on children created beneath it |
| **May route** | `bankai:agent/*` on **children it creates**, by scope (§ 3) |
| **No `Wake` row** | Hatsu has no *CI builder* to re-fire; a wake on a PR's other automated participant is [`sharingan`](../sharingan/SKILL.md)'s |
| **Never** | routes the named issue itself (§ 3 **asks** — its mode is the maintainer's read), applies a G1 mode label, merges, votes or publishes — § 10 |

**The delegation expires when the run ends. Say when it ends.**

## 6. When it will not move

No CI-wake ladder exists for Kurapika's own build: a stall is reported plainly, in-session — the
blocker, and whether it needs the maintainer.

- **A released issue this session could not finish** is `🔵 on hold`, naming the blocker — never
  silently abandoned.
- **Where Hatsu cannot do the work at all, that is a G5 naming the gap**, not a routing decision.
- **Filing is a legitimate outcome**: a real defect elsewhere blocking delivery is filed with
  [`file`](../file/SKILL.md), linked, and the build held on it.

## 7. Reporting and the stop

**The six-step verified-delivery checklist and the four claims are
[`docs/WORKFLOW.md`](../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § *Verified delivery — the coordinator's four
claims***, owed in full before any handover, delegated work included.

**The reviewer-round policy is [`sharingan`](../sharingan/SKILL.md) § 6's**, never restated here.
Progress turns and gate stops are [PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Reporting a phase*'s; a
progress line names the issue, mode, PR, checks and rounds, and what is next.

| Gate | When | The ask |
|---|---|---|
| **G1** | an epic awaits its mode label (row `mode-label`) | `DECIDE`, with the trade-off |
| **G2/G4** | the delivery PR is `CON-32`-Ready (rows `merge`, `canon-merge`) | `MERGE`, the verdict saying everything |
| **G5** | a stuck local build, or a capability a local session cannot have | `DECIDE` or `DO` with a proposed issue — a mode tie is row `mode-unknown`; a missing installable tool, row `missing-tool`, is installed, not asked |

The run **ends** when the delivery PR stands Ready, the issue closes, or at a G5 it cannot pass: say
which, and that the delegation has lapsed.

## 8. Resuming

[PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Resuming a run*; § 2's `chain-position` is idempotent, and
`docs/Loop/<run-id>/` holds decisions, every logged label application and each build session's
progress.

## 9. Residue

- **Severity/mode reasoning, § 3's `DECIDE` brief and § 6's G5 diagnosis** stay judgment.
- **One stage label per object** (`CON-9`) is not enforced: `nen label apply` applies and logs the
  one label it is given.
- **A repository with no `project` block** is built with its own documented commands, said so; the
  declaration is its own change at the declaration gate.
- **The stage-free path's raw issue read** (§ 1) is never a chain verdict, and **`nen issue
  edit-body`'s whole-body write is not conditional**: a concurrent change goes to the discovery
  protocol, never claimed as an atomic replacement.

## 10. Hard limits

- **Never merges `main`** (`CON-5`/`CON-7`, rows `merge`/`canon-merge`), its own PR anywhere, or the
  chore/integration delivery PR.
- **Never applies a G1 mode label**, inside a run or outside it, and never routes the entry issue
  without an answer.
- **Never votes, self-reviews, impersonates a reviewer, or casts `request_changes`** (`CON-26`).
- **Never drives more than two efforts at once** (`--local-cap 2`), or lets two children touch one file.
- **Never claims a CI builder is doing the work** — Kurapika builds it, said plainly.
- **Never builds, tests or lints a declared repository from a remembered command line**, and never
  manufactures a `--chain-labels` map or a stage label a repository lacks.
- **Never runs `nen shu deploy --run`** — a G3 act; this run stops at G2/G4.
- **Never publishes a release** — G3 is the maintainer's (`CON-6`, row `release-go`).
- **Never leaves the delegation open** — say when it ends.
